topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
consensus_response: Interleaved array element spacing significantly impacts coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links. Closer spacings improve gain but increase side lobes, potentially introducing grating lobes that can degrade isolation. Conversely, wider spacings decrease side lobes but compromise XPDR performance due to reduced element density. Optimal spacing balances these trade-offs while ensuring low inter-element interference and high gain for efficient frequency reuse and coverage in Ka-band satellite links.
reference_context: Ka-band satellites employ spot beam coverage allowing frequency reuse operation with implications on antenna design, including the use of planar arrays and phased arrays to achieve larger apertures and directivity.
